name: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
problem: For autoregressive decode the KV cache is the memory bottleneck, and it gets worse with context length, batch size and every KV head - GQA reduces it only by an integer factor while the cache still scales linearly in sequence length.
mechanism: Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA). Down-project the concatenated per-head K and V into a single low-dimensional latent vector (much smaller than the K+V total), CACHE ONLY THE LATENT, and up-project back to per-head K and V at attention time. Absorption of the up-projection into the query lets decode-time attention read the small latent directly without materialising per-head K/V, so the cache is compressed by the projection rank rather than by dropping heads. Plus DeepSeekMoE: fine-grained expert segmentation plus shared experts, and load-balancing auxiliary losses.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract), all vs DeepSeek 67B: saves 42.5% of training cost, reduces the KV cache by 93.3%, and boosts maximum generation throughput by 5.76x. These are three different quantities (cost, memory, throughput) against one named baseline - not interchangeable, and the KV-cache and throughput numbers are the two that matter for serving. Trained on 8.1T tokens with 21B activated parameters.

MERGED FIELD BY FIELD - nothing was silently dropped:
  mechanism: the retired record's text was materially fuller (803 chars vs 573) and is RETAINED here rather than discarded. Its text: Combines two independent mechanisms. (1) DeepSeekMoE: fine-grained mN experts with mK activated plus K_s always-on shared experts; 236B total, 21B activated per token, 128K context. (2) Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA): instead of caching K and V per KV head, project the hidden state once per token down to a low-dimensional latent, cache ONLY that latent, then up-project to per-head K and V at attention time, with decoupled RoPE applied to a separate small vector so positional information survives the down-projection. Per-token KV cache becomes O(d_c) instead of O(L * d_h * d_k) and, crucially, INDEPENDENT of the number of KV heads, so raising head count for quality no longer multiplies cache size. MLA is the mechanism that changes the serving memory bottleneck; the MoE block alone does not.

The inference-side MLA claim is reported as a KV-cache size reduction rather than a tokens/second number, so there is no serving throughput figure to quote. Reported on H800 GPUs, a China-market SKU close to H100 SXM compute."
